title: Art direction reference — t1energy.com
purpose: A reading of the reference site's visual system, abstracted to principles and tokens, then translated for the Homer City Energy Campus site. This is an art-direction brief, not a clone target. Anything marked in `doNotCopy` is T1's property or T1's meaning and must not travel.

source.designedBy: MOUTHWASH Studio (identity + site), logo with Moniker, T1 Sans by Daniel Wenzel at 26A1

capture.reason: t1energy.com and every published case-study domain are egress-blocked in this environment. v1.0.0 of this file was reconstructed from search-indexed case-study prose. The client then supplied four direct screenshots of the live site, which corrected several structural readings — see `corrections`.
screenshotsSupplied: Hero with Discover button and announcement card
Technology section — accordion with circular controls
Company section — stat treatment and rounded media
Expanded navigation — mega-menu panel with grouped children and two footer CTAs
Blog index — control bar, three-column grid, byline meta and category chips
capture.confidence: high on layout, radius, colour temperature, component form and type treatment; medium on exact pixel metrics, which are still Homer City decisions rather than measurements
stillUnverified: Exact hex values and type sizes — estimated from screenshots at unknown scale
Section order across the full homepage
Motion and hover behaviour, which no still frame can show
Whether the neon green accent the case study describes appears anywhere in these views — it does not

evidence.claim: Modular grid system pulled from T1's primary output — solar cells. Individual blocks act as building components across the identity: they form the logomark, generate the icon library, and structure the website UI.
The mark is constructed from a grid of solar-inspired blocks reflecting strength, resilience, flexibility and scale.
T1 Sans is a bespoke typeface juxtaposing round and sharp edges, drawn from the 'T' and '1' letterforms. The tension reads as static in print and resolves through motion in digital.
The round-to-sharp transition is experienced through UX details and subtle hover states on the website.
Palette is reserved, with 'quiet confidence', deliberately avoiding the bright reds and oranges that read as hazard in industrial settings. A neon green accent replaces renewable-energy forest green.
Process and innovation are explained visually rather than verbally. The design is 'deep with detail without feeling dense'.
Block-based page architecture: mission, manufacturing (cell to module), supply chain, layer-by-layer technology detail, key figures, news feed.

Homepage hero copy is a single declarative sentence of what the company builds and why: 'T1 Energy is building domestic solar & battery supply chains to invigorate America with scalable, reliable, and low cost energy.'

thesis: The reference resolves a hard industrial subject into something a non-expert can read, by making the company's own unit of production the unit of the layout. Everything is a block; blocks tile into an array; the array is the page. Brutalist structure, softened only where a human touches it. Explanation happens visually, in sequence, not in paragraphs.

principles.name: The product is the grid
principles.reference: A solar cell tiles into a module; a module tiles into an array. That geometry is the logo, the icon set, and the page layout.
principles.translation: Homer City's unit is not a solar cell — copying one would be borrowing T1's meaning. Our unit is the campus parcel: a 3,200-acre site laid out as a survey grid of functional blocks (power block, GIS, compressor station, water treatment, mod yard, data center campus). The page tiles the same way the site does.
principles.test: If a module could be swapped for a square of any other brand's product and mean the same thing, the motif is decorative and should be cut.

principles.name: Show the process, don't describe it
principles.reference: Cell to module to array; layer-by-layer PV construction — taught in pictures and sequence, not prose.
principles.translation: Demolition to foundation to first steel to turbine set. The July 2026 photo essay already is this sequence. Gas in, turbine, HRSG, grid out is the same move for the power block. Neither needs a paragraph.
principles.test: A neighbour should understand what is being built having read only the eyebrow labels.

principles.name: Reserved palette, one accent, no hazard colour
principles.reference: Restrained neutrals; bright red and orange avoided because they carry hazard meaning on an industrial site; one contemporary accent.
principles.translation: Adopt wholesale, and it is sharper here than at T1: this is an active construction site where red and amber are live safety signals. Reserve them strictly for the alert banner's Construction and Urgent severities so they still mean something. Our single accent is the seeded blue.
principles.test: Count the saturated colours visible in one viewport. More than one and something is decorative.

principles.name: Softness is radius, and it is generous
principles.reference: A pill-shaped translucent nav floating over the media; ~32-40px corners on every photograph and card; fully circular +/− controls. Almost nothing in the layout is square.
principles.translation: Adopt directly. Media and cards take radius/media (32); every control is a pill or a circle. The "brutalism" half of the phrase lives in the type and the bare open ground, not in sharp corners.
principles.test: A square corner anywhere in the layout is a bug. The only hard edges are the edges of the viewport.

principles.name: Deep with detail, without density
principles.reference: A great deal of technical information, paced so it never reads as a wall.
principles.translation: The sceptic needs sources, dates and footnotes on the page — CLAUDE.md section 5 requires it. Pacing is what stops that from becoming a document dump: one idea per module, generous field around each, footnotes bound to their own figure rather than pooled at the page foot.
principles.test: Every module states one thing. If it states two, it is two modules.

principles.name: Open ground, not containers
principles.reference: Content sits directly on one continuous warm off-white ground. Sections are separated by space alone — no cards, no rules, no tinted bands, no gutters.
principles.translation: Adopt directly. The only filled surfaces in the system are translucent overlays floating on media (nav, announcement card) and the dark footer. Everything else is type and photographs on bare ground.
principles.test: Delete every filled rectangle that is not a photograph or an overlay. If the page still reads, it was built right.

doNotCopy: T1 Sans. Bespoke, licensed to T1, and drawn from their own letterforms. We use Geist.
The neon green accent. It is T1's single most identifying colour and carries their sustainability argument. Our accent is the seeded blue.
The solar-cell motif and any cell/wafer/module iconography. It is a literal picture of T1's product and means nothing here.
The cell-to-module-to-array explanatory diagram as a form. The idea (P2) travels; the specific diagram does not.
Any copy. The hero sentence quoted above is evidence of structure only.

palette.note: Seeds supplied by the client as swatch images on 2026-09-13. Hex values below are visually sampled from those images and MUST be confirmed against the source file before build — see openQuestions.OQ-A1. Every ramp step is derived from a seed; every pairing below is contrast-computed, not estimated.

seeds.blueNote: The original seed blue #3F74AB no longer anchors the ramp and currently has no semantic role. Confirm whether it is retired or reassigned.

contrastFindings.finding: The seeded mid-gray #808080 (ink/700) reaches only 3.95:1 on white. It cannot carry body text.
contrastFindings.consequence: ink/700 is demoted to a 3:1 role — large text, icon marks, UI edges. A new step ink/750 (#66666A) was interpolated to carry metadata and eyebrows: 5.72:1 on white, 5.24:1 on paper, 4.88:1 on the ink/100 field. ink/750 is the AA floor for neutral text in this system.
contrastFindings.rule: Nothing lighter than ink/750 may carry text on any ground.

contrastFindings.finding: White on navy blue/950 is 16.52:1; blue/200 on navy is 10.22:1.
contrastFindings.consequence: Navy bands have full headroom for both primary and secondary inverse text.

contrastFindings.finding: The signal colours are derived, not seeded. None of the three appears in the client's swatches.
contrastFindings.consequence: They exist only because a construction-alert banner needs three distinguishable severities and the seeds offer no warm hue at all.
contrastFindings.rule: Flagged for client sign-off — see openQuestions.OQ-A2. They appear nowhere except the alert banner.

contrastFindings.finding: Against the new warm off-white ground ink/100 (#EDEDEC): ink/950 is 14.37:1, ink/800 is 6.20:1, ink/750 is 4.88:1, blue/600 is 5.27:1.
contrastFindings.consequence: Every text role clears AA on the single ground. ink/700 (#808080) is 3.62:1 there and remains non-text only.
contrastFindings.rule: ink/750 stays the AA floor for neutral text. Muted accordion rows at rest may use ink/700 ONLY when they are large text (≥24px), where 3:1 applies.

contrastFindings.finding: The supplied action colour #0C73CD is 4.83:1 on white but only 4.12:1 on the #EDEDEC page ground.
contrastFindings.consequence: It clears AA as a button fill — white on it is 4.83:1 — but fails as link text on the page ground, which is where most links live.
contrastFindings.rule: action/primary-bg = blue/600 (#0C73CD), the supplied colour, used filled. text/link = blue/700 (#0A5CA3) at 5.83:1 on the ground and 6.83:1 on white. text/link-inverse = blue/500 (#1A8DF2) at 4.92:1 on the near-black footer.

contrastFindings.finding: blue/500 (#1A8DF2) reaches 3.42:1 under white, 2.92:1 on the ink/100 ground, and 4.92:1 on the ink/950 band.
contrastFindings.consequence: One blue cannot do all three jobs. The ramp splits by ground: blue/600 fills buttons (white label 4.83:1), blue/700 carries link text on light ground (5.83:1), blue/500 carries link text on the dark bands (4.92:1) where the darker steps collapse to 3.49:1 and 2.46:1.
contrastFindings.rule: action/primary-bg = blue/600. text/link = blue/700. text/link-inverse = blue/500. A link that changes ground changes step.

contrastFindings.finding: The hero overlay panels run at 50%, not 62%. Measured against a pure-white photograph through the hero scrim, the weakest point of the nav capsule is 5.73:1 and of the announcement card 5.56:1 under white text.
contrastFindings.consequence: 50% holds for white, but ink/300 metadata on the same panel falls to 3.64:1 because the scrim has decayed to 0.33 by the right edge of the frame.
contrastFindings.rule: Secondary text on a translucent panel over media uses text/on-overlay-secondary (ink/100, 4.75:1), not text/inverse-secondary. The two are different problems: solid ink has 10:1 of headroom, a 50% panel over a bright photograph has none.

contrastFindings.finding: text/muted at ink/700 passed only by the large-text exemption. Accordion rows are 26px on desktop (3:1 applies, 3.37:1 passes) and 20px on mobile (4.5:1 applies, 3.37:1 fails).
contrastFindings.consequence: Twenty accordion labels failed on the mobile boards while the identical desktop rows passed. A responsive type ramp can move real copy across the large-text threshold without anything visibly changing.
contrastFindings.rule: text/muted = ink/750. Check AA at the smallest mode a token renders in, not the largest.

contrastFindings.finding: text/meta (ink/750) reaches 4.88:1 on the ink/100 page ground but only 4.29:1 on the ink/200 placeholder field.
contrastFindings.consequence: Production briefs set inside image placeholders sat just under the floor — 17 of them across both breakpoints.
contrastFindings.rule: On surface/field, metadata steps to text/secondary (ink/800, 5.33:1).

contrastFindings.finding: The timeline's quiet date pill needed a filled mid-grey carrying a 12px white label. ink/700 is the obvious mid step and fails at 3.95:1.
contrastFindings.consequence: ink/750 is the lightest step that clears 4.5:1 against white, at 5.72:1 — the same step the text floor landed on, arrived at from the opposite direction.
contrastFindings.rule: surface/marker-quiet = ink/750. The neutral floor governs a ground carrying light text exactly as it governs text on a light ground.

groundRules: One ground: ink/100 (#EDEDEC), a warm off-white, runs the length of every page. It is not a section device — it is the paper.
White is not the page. It appears only inside circular icon buttons and the rare raised card.
No coloured bands. No navy. The client direction is explicit: blue lives on links and CTAs and nowhere else.
The footer is ink/950 near-black rather than navy — institutional weight without introducing a second hue.
Overlays on media are translucent near-black with a blur, never a solid fill.

typography.note: T1 Sans is bespoke and unavailable. Geist is the closest available register. Heading weights are set lighter than the previous pass — the reference sets headlines and stats at Regular and Light, which is most of what makes the pages feel open.

mono.role: the technical register — module labels, coordinates, figure units, 'as of' stamps, file metadata, milestone dates

typography.monoRationale: The reference explains a technical subject without technical prose. A mono face does that job structurally: it marks a string as instrument-read rather than written. Here it carries exactly the things CLAUDE.md section 5 requires to be visible and dated — the 'as of September 2026' stamp, footnote markers, permit numbers, file sizes. It makes provenance look like provenance.
typography.case: Sentence case everywhere, including mono labels. The reference sets section and stat labels in mono ALL-CAPS preceded by a small filled square; this design takes neither. The mono face alone carries the technical register.
typography.responsive: Only font size varies by breakpoint, carried by a Desktop/Mobile mode on the Typography collection. Line height and tracking are percentages so they scale on their own. Set the mode on the artboard, never per node.
typography.labelMark: None. Section labels are mono text with no preceding mark. The reference's square bullet was built and then removed at the client's direction — see `clientDirection.labelMark`.

bandWidths.note: Band width comes from the parent's horizontal padding, never from the band itself.

radius.note: Principle P4 — softness is radius, applied broadly.

asymmetry.rule: The content column sits right of centre. The left half is empty, or holds a single rounded image, or carries provenance set small.
asymmetry.why: Emptiness is the reference's primary compositional device, and here it earns a second job: the empty column is where footnotes, "as of" stamps and source lines live without crowding the thing they qualify.

rhythm.rule: A section states one thing and is broken when it outgrows roughly one and a half viewports. Length is not depth — a long section is usually two sections that have not been separated yet.
rhythm.howToSplit: Split a long stat run by theme rather than by count. The homepage seven-figure block became "what the build is worth to people who live here" (jobs and investment) and "how big it is" (site and scale), which is a more useful division than four-and-three.
rhythm.sectionPadding: 120px top and bottom for gridded sections, 160px for asymmetric editorial ones. The image band supplies its own break and needs no extra padding around it.
rhythm.imageCadence: Roughly one full-bleed band every three or four sections. Two per page is the ceiling.

alertBanner.role: Global, CMS-driven, above the header. The client's fastest lever.
alertBanner.treatment: Full-bleed band. Severity changes the ground colour and the mono label only — layout, type size and dismiss affordance never move.
alertBanner.behaviour: Dismissible, dismissal remembered per visitor, a new alert reappears. Scheduled start/end dates. role=status, never traps focus.

header.role: No bar. Two independent floating elements over the hero media.
header.logo: Standalone at top-left, x=48 y=32, set in mark/inverse directly on the photograph. No container.

navPill.form: Rounded bar at radius/chrome (16), height 47, translucent surface/overlay-strong at 50% with a 24px blur. Not a pill — client direction 2026-09-13. The capsule only materialises over media; on the dark inner-page bands it dissolves into the ground and the items read as plain text.
navPill.position: top-right, x from right margin 48, y 32
navPill.externalMarker: A trailing ↗ marks any item that leaves the site

header.cta: The Jobs button sits as a separate pill immediately right of the nav capsule, filled action/primary-bg — the one saturated element in the viewport.
header.innerPages: On grounds without hero media the capsule becomes solid surface/inverse so it keeps its contrast.
header.mobile: Logo left, a single Menu pill right carrying a 3×3 dot-grid icon. The Jobs pill stays visible beside it.

megaMenu.form: The bar expands downward into a second panel at radius/overlay (32), separated by an 8px gap, same width as the bar.
megaMenu.ground: surface/overlay-panel — ink/950 at 86%, darker than the bar's 50%, so dimmed children clear AA.
megaMenu.columns: One column per top-level item, aligned under its parent. Children in text/inverse-secondary; the bar stays white.
megaMenu.footer: Two full-width CTA pills, label left and arrow pushed to the right edge.
megaMenu.accessibility: Opens on hover AND on focus/click, closes on Escape, and every child is in the tab order. Hover is never the only path.

hero.treatment: Full-bleed photograph, scrim, real text over it. Headline at font-size/h2 (44 desktop / 30 mobile) rather than display — client direction 2026-09-13. No lead sentence: the orientation section below carries it. Two buttons, the filled one first. Announcement cards float bottom-right on desktop and stack under the copy on mobile.
hero.scrim: Set so the weakest point over the text column clears AA against a pure white photograph — desktop 0.72 at the end of the text column, mobile 0.88 throughout. A contrast checker cannot verify this: it walks to the nearest solid painted ancestor and a photograph is not one. Do not lighten.
hero.mediaLabel: Every hero carries a mono kind/date label — 'Photograph · July 2026' or 'Rendering'. Required, not decorative: the deck's cover is a render of a campus that does not exist yet.

sequence.role: The P2 device, built as the Timeline stage component set: one dated milestone on a shared vertical axis.
sequence.treatment: A date pill sits centred on the axis; a 1px rail drops from it; the copy — title over one or two lines of body — sits 48px clear of the axis and alternates side to side down the page. No thumbnail, no container, no rule around the copy. The pill and the rail are the only filled shapes in the section.

variants.Side: Left | Right | Stacked. Left and Right alternate down the desktop spine. Stacked is the 375px form.
variants.State: Current | Past. Exactly one stage per timeline is Current — the most recent milestone.

states.Current: Pill surface/inverse with text/inverse; rail surface/inverse.
states.Past: Pill and rail both surface/marker-quiet, pill label text/inverse.
states.bodyCopy: text/secondary in both states. The reference dims the body copy of past items as well as their markers. This is a transparency timeline and the evidence does not get dimmed — only the marker changes.

metrics.axis: Dead centre of the 1280 container, held by two FILL spacers either side of the pill, so the axis does not move when a date string gets longer.
metrics.pill: 12px mono, 3% tracking, 8/16 padding, radius/pill. 32px tall — which puts the centre of its left cap at x=16.
metrics.copyColumn: 400px fixed, 48px clear of the axis. Right-aligned on the left of the spine, left-aligned on the right.
metrics.rhythm: 24px pill to rail, 24px rail to the next pill, and the rail overruns the copy by 24px at each end so it reads as a rail rather than an underline.
metrics.title: font-size/h4 Medium, down from the 28px h3 the column form used. The pill is the loud element; the title is subordinate to it.

sequence.heading: Centred — eyebrow, headline and spine share one axis, and the headline is held to 840px so it breaks like the reference's. This is the only centred heading in the system; every other section heading stays left. A centred spine under a left-aligned heading has nothing to hang from.
sequence.replaces: The four-across column form, which carried a 260px image slot per step. The same placeholder photograph appeared four times in a row in every timeline, and the production brief inside each slot was repeated with it — 16 slots and 16 briefs across the two breakpoints.
sequence.stillToBuild: The 1969–2023 photo essay and the gas → turbine → HRSG → grid out explainer were both slated for this device and neither is built. The photo essay is image-led and should not reuse the stage as it now stands.

primary.note: The only saturated element on a page.

overlay.note: Over media only — the hero Discover-style control.

quiet.note: Hairline ink/300 edge. Used on the open ground.

button.metrics: Vertical padding space/8, horizontal space/24, radius/pill. Height follows the label's line box: 43 desktop, 41 mobile. Client direction 2026-09-13 — the button reads as a line of type in a capsule, not a slab.

footer.treatment: ink/950 near-black band, radius 0 (it meets the viewport edge). Four contact routes kept distinct — the brief specifies four inboxes and they must not collapse into one form. Carries the two standing footnotes.

announcementCard.role: Floating card at bottom-right of the hero. Carries the single most current thing on the site.
announcementCard.form: Translucent surface/overlay-strong at 50%, radius/overlay (32), 16px padding, blurred. Thumbnail at radius/thumb (16) — 109px desktop, 96px mobile so the headline keeps a readable measure. The card hugs its copy; it never holds a fixed height.
announcementCard.contents: Sentence-case mono label carrying category and date, then a two-to-three-line headline in text/inverse, then the thumbnail. The label is text/on-overlay-secondary, not text/inverse-secondary — see contrastFindings.
announcementCard.homerCityUse: This is the right home for the construction-update banner the brief requires — it is more current-feeling than a full-width strip and it does not push the hero down. Urgent severity is the exception: it takes a full-width bar above everything, because a blasting notice must not be dismissible furniture.

statOpen.role: Every stat array on the site. No container, no rule — figures sit on the open ground in a grid.
statOpen.form: Figure at 96px Light in text/stat-figure. A mono qualifier line above it, a mono label beneath, and a footnote slot beneath that.

grid.twoUp: 620px cells, 40px gutter, 56-88px row gap. Used in a full-width band (1280 content) for figures with long labels or required footnotes.
grid.threeUp: 400px cells, 40px gutter, 56px row gap. Used for short figures with short labels.
grid.never: A single vertical stack. Seven figures stacked ran 1,768px on the homepage and read as a list rather than a set.

statOpen.baselineRule: The qualifier line reserves its space even when a figure has no qualifier, so every figure in a row sits on a common baseline. In Webflow this is a min-height on the qualifier element, not an empty text node.
rules: The qualifier (Up to / Projected / Anticipated) sits ABOVE the figure, never buried mid-label.
A volatile figure carries its "as of" date as the qualifier — the eyebrow is where a date-stamp lives.
Required footnotes sit in full inside the cell, beneath the label. Not an asterisk, not a pointer to the page foot.
Figures are near-black, never blue — blue means link.
Never round a figure for visual balance.

accordion.role: FAQ, the trades roster, commitments, and the power-block explainer.
accordion.form: Rows on open ground with no dividers. Row label at accordion-row size. A circular white icon button sits at the right of each row carrying + when closed and − when open.
accordion.states: Closed rows sit in text/muted (ink/700, permissible at 26px where the 3:1 large-text threshold applies); the open row moves to text/primary.
accordion.accessibility: The circular control is a real button with an accessible name, not a decorative glyph. Rows are keyboard reachable and every answer stays in the DOM.

blogIndex.controlBar: A row of label:value controls — Filter: All types · Sort by: Most recent · View: Grid 3 col. Label in text/primary, value in text/meta, small chevron. Mono throughout.
blogIndex.card: Media at radius/media, then a meta line (date in text/primary, separator, issuer in text/meta), then the headline at H3, then a category chip.
blogIndex.chip: Pill at surface/field with text/secondary. Categories: Workforce · Construction · Community · Permits.
blogIndex.types: Three content types in one collection — press release, media statement, supportive coverage. Coverage items link out and credit the outlet.

imageBand.role: Full-bleed photographic break between sections. The main device for stopping a page reading as one long column.
imageBand.form: 1440 x 520 image area meeting both viewport edges, then a caption row inside the 80px page margin.
imageBand.corners: Square. This is the one place hard edges are correct under P4 — the image meets the viewport edge, which is the only hard edge the system allows.
imageBand.caption: A mono kind label (Photograph or Rendering, plus date) and a caption, both OUTSIDE the image area. The production brief sits INSIDE it, in the region a real photograph destroys.
imageBand.spend: Spent, not spread: never two adjacent, and no more than two per page.
imageBand.placeholder: All photographic slots currently carry one placeholder image supplied by the client. Because each slot has a different aspect ratio, FILL crops it differently and no two read as the same frame — but this is one asset standing in for many. Every slot needs its own photograph in production, and the brief inside each slot says which.
imageBand.briefChip: The production brief sits on a translucent chip inside the image area so it stays legible over any photograph, light or dark. Without it the note disappears against the very thing it is describing.

motion.reference: The round-to-sharp tension of the letterforms resolves through motion; hover states carry the detail.
motion.translation: Motion resolves structure, it does not decorate. Modules settle into their array on reveal; the hairline gutter is what animates. Nothing overshoots.
constraints: Stays inside Webflow Interactions 2.0 where possible: scroll-into-view, scroll-progress, hover, page-load, click. Anything richer needs a GSAP embed and an explicit call-out.

imagery.reference: Industrial subject matter shot plainly; explanation carried visually.
imagery.translation: The client's aerial and landscape frames are the strongest asset in the source material — the campus set in Indiana County farmland, with the town in shot. This imagery is what makes the site read as a place rather than a company.
rules: Square corners on all media. Radius is for controls only.
Every image carries a mono kind label: Photograph or Rendering. Non-negotiable — see CLAUDE.md section 7.
Date is a structured field, never part of the caption string.
Production notes and published captions never share a field. A brief lives inside the image area the photograph will destroy; the caption lives outside it.
Full bleed is spent, not spread: never two photographic bands adjacent.
Explicit dimensions, lazy loading below the fold, modern formats. Rural county, mobile-first, constrained connections. No layout shift.

sectionArchetypes.name: Hero
sectionArchetypes.from: T1 hero — one declarative sentence over full-bleed media

sectionArchetypes.name: Orientation
sectionArchetypes.note: Three short paragraphs: what, where, what stage now.

sectionArchetypes.name: Stat sequence
sectionArchetypes.note: Open ground, one stat per row, provenance in the empty column.

sectionArchetypes.name: Statement
sectionArchetypes.note: Was an institutional navy band in v1. Now type on bare ground — the emphasis comes from scale and surrounding emptiness.

sectionArchetypes.name: Editorial split
sectionArchetypes.note: Media one side, text the other.

supersedes.note: This art direction changes four standing rules in CLAUDE.md section 7. Each is a deliberate consequence of the reference, flagged for the user's decision — not a silent override.

changes.rule: CLAUDE.md section 7 — 'And no cards: a filled box is not a grouping device.'
changes.change: The module array is the reference's core structural device and cannot be adopted without filled boxes.
changes.reconciliation: The original rule targets decorative white cards floating on a light ground — 2015-era boxing that does what space already does. Our module inverts that: the module is white and the GROUND is tinted, the gap between modules is field showing through rather than a drawn border, and nothing is stroked, shadowed or rounded. The rule's intent — no decorative boxing — is kept; its letter is not.

changes.rule: CLAUDE.md section 7 — 'No tinted grounds; the sand family is used by no semantic role.'
changes.change: A tinted field (ink/100) is now load-bearing: it is what makes module gutters visible.
changes.reconciliation: It is a neutral from the client's own seeded gray ramp, not a warm sand wash, and it is structural rather than decorative.

changes.rule: CLAUDE.md section 7 — 'stone/700 is the floor for neutral text.'
changes.change: Under the new seeds the equivalent step fails AA at 3.95:1. The floor moves to ink/750 (#66666A).
changes.reconciliation: The rule's intent (a hard AA floor for neutral text) is unchanged; only the step that satisfies it moved, because the seeds moved.

changes.rule: CLAUDE.md section 7 — implicitly a single type family.
changes.change: Geist Mono is added as a second family for the technical/provenance register.
changes.reconciliation: It carries the date stamps, footnote markers and source metadata that section 5 already requires to be visible. It makes a fact-discipline requirement legible as a design signal.

unchanged: All of CLAUDE.md section 5 (fact discipline) and section 6 (canonical figures) apply without modification.
'Blue means link' holds — the accent is blue/600 and nothing else is blue, icons included.
A pillar colour marks one of the four pillars and nothing else.
WCAG 2.2 AA, non-negotiable. Rollovers need a non-hover path.
Mobile is the primary comp for the responsive pass.

openQuestions.question: Confirm the seed hex values. The palette was supplied as swatch images and the values here are visually sampled: blue #3F74AB, paper #F5F5F5, and a seven-step gray ramp #F8F8F8 → #1D1D1F.
openQuestions.blocks: Build. A one-degree error in the blue changes which step is the link colour.

openQuestions.question: Sign off the three derived signal colours (construction #A9610B, urgent #9E2A22, affirm #2F6B4F). None is seeded — the seeds contain no warm hue, and a construction-alert banner needs three distinguishable severities.
Does regrouping FAQ & Resources and News under a single Newsroom parent stand? It changes the approved Stage 2 sitemap.
The seed blue #3F74AB no longer has a role now that #0C73CD anchors the ramp. Retire it, or give it one?
openQuestions.blocks: Nothing — flagged so it is a decision rather than a silent drop.

openQuestions.question: Are the mega-menu children anchor links inside their parent page, or separate routes? The nav implies routes; the comps currently build them as sections.
openQuestions.blocks: URL map and the remaining page comps

openQuestions.question: The hero placeholder is a data-centre interior, but the campus data centres are not built yet — so it is almost certainly stock or a rendering. The hero currently labels itself "Photograph · July 2026". Confirm the kind label before launch.
openQuestions.blocks: Launch. This is open question 10 in CLAUDE.md made concrete.

openQuestions.question: Does this art direction supersede the client's five-colour brand palette (navy #143251, blue #238FC8, aqua #AFECF1, cream #F3F1D0, gold #D8B471) recorded in CLAUDE.md section 7, or sit alongside it? The new seeds share neither the aqua, the cream nor the gold.
Capture t1energy.com directly. Every metric in this file is a Homer City decision, not a measurement — the reference was reconstructed from case-study text because the domain is egress-blocked here.
openQuestions.blocks: Nothing. Would raise confidence from inference to measurement.

openQuestions.question: Geist stands in for the bespoke T1 Sans. If the brand guide (CLAUDE.md open question #1) names a real typeface, it replaces Geist and the whole scale re-points to it.
openQuestions.blocks: Nothing — the scale is tokenised and re-points in one change.

openQuestions.question: Is the fourth nav item 'Media' or 'Newsroom'? The client typed 'Media' over the hero instance on 2026-09-13; it has been propagated to the component and all fourteen instances across both breakpoints.
openQuestions.note: Related to OQ-A6. 'Newsroom' was the parent that grouped News with FAQ & Resources; 'Media' reads narrower and may not want FAQ under it.

openQuestions.question: The two hero announcement cards carry identical copy under different dates (9/24 and 9/21), and both dates are ahead of today.
openQuestions.note: Mirrored to mobile as-is rather than invented around. Two real construction updates are needed, or the hero should carry one card.

openQuestions.question: Contact had a page hero on the mobile board and none on desktop. It has been restored on desktop from the mobile copy so the two match and Contact matches the other six pages.
openQuestions.blocks: Nothing — flagged so it can be removed if it was deliberately cut.

openQuestions.question: The Campus timeline dated "on-site headcount crosses 1,000" to March 2026. No client document gives a March 2026 headcount — the earliest dated count anywhere is ~1,300 as of May 2026.
openQuestions.note: The figure was an interpolation between dated counts, which §5.1 forbids. Removed while rebuilding the stage; the milestone now reads "Construction workforce mobilized with Kiewit Power Constructors and the local building trades", which is sourced. A real March 2026 count restores it.

openQuestions.question: The Campus page's "Full timeline" promises every dated milestone, lists four, and they are not the four the homepage teaser lists. Home shows first steel (April 2026) and Unit 5 HRSG (July 2026); The Campus shows workforce mobilization (March 2026) and full construction (June 2026). Neither set contains the other.
openQuestions.blocks: The Campus — Full timeline, Home — Timeline
openQuestions.note: A homepage teaser should be a subset of the page it teases, and a heading that says "every" has to mean it. The tour deck's photo essay carries more dated milestones than either page shows. Needs the client's milestone list.

corrections.v1Claim: The page is built from a hard modular grid of square white blocks separated by 1px gutters.
corrections.reality: The modular grid lives in the LOGO and the icon set. The page itself is open, asymmetric and nearly empty — content sits directly on the ground with almost no containers at all.
corrections.cause: The case study’s phrase "individual blocks structure the website’s UI design" was read as page layout. It describes the identity system.
corrections.impact: Load-bearing. The entire module-array device is removed.

corrections.v1Claim: "Brutalism and softness" means square structure with radius reserved for controls.
corrections.reality: Softness IS radius, applied broadly and generously — a pill-shaped floating nav, ~32-40px on photographs and cards, fully circular +/− buttons. Very little in the layout is square.
corrections.cause: Inverted reading of the same phrase.
corrections.impact: Load-bearing. Radius roles re-pointed from 0/6 to 32/pill.

corrections.v1Claim: The header is a solid white bar with a hairline base rule.
corrections.reality: There is no bar. The logo sits alone at top-left directly on the hero media, and the nav is a translucent, blurred, pill-shaped capsule floating at top-right. A "Menu" pill with a 3×3 dot-grid icon appears on inner pages.

corrections.v1Claim: Two grounds alternate — warm neutral for reading, navy for institutional moments.
corrections.reality: The site is effectively monochrome: one warm off-white ground throughout, near-black type, white and translucent-dark overlays. No coloured institutional bands. The neon green the case study describes appears in none of the supplied views.
corrections.cause: Carried over from the previous Homer City design pass rather than read from the reference.
corrections.impact: Navy bands removed. Client direction: blue is reserved for links and CTAs only.

corrections.v1Claim: Stat figures sit inside white modules in a tiled array.
corrections.reality: Stat figures are very large, light-weight, and sit on the open ground with a small mono label directly beneath. No container, no array, no rules. They are separated by vertical space alone.
corrections.impact: Stat component rebuilt on open ground; figure size raised 72 → 96.

corrections.v1Claim: Sections run full-width with even columns.
corrections.reality: Layout is strongly asymmetric. The left half of the screen is frequently empty or holds a single rounded image; the content column sits right of centre. Emptiness is the primary compositional device.
corrections.impact: Grid re-specified as an asymmetric two-column system.

corrections.reality: T1 sets them as mono ALL-CAPS preceded by a small filled square — "■ TECHNOLOGY", "■ COMPANY" — and uses the same mono caps for every stat label.
corrections.impact: Neither adopted. CLAUDE.md §7 forbids all-caps and the client chose to keep that rule; the square bullet was built and then removed at the client's direction. Labels are mono, sentence case, unmarked.

corrections.v1Claim: The nav is a flat list of links.
corrections.reality: The bar expands downward into a second rounded panel. Each top-level item is a parent whose children sit in a column directly beneath it. Children are dimmed relative to the bar. The panel closes with two full-width CTA pills, arrows pushed to the far right edge.
corrections.cause: Only the collapsed state was visible in the earlier screenshots.
corrections.impact: Nav rebuilt as a mega-menu; site IA regrouped to match — see `informationArchitecture`.

corrections.v1Claim: The news index is a plain grid of cards.
corrections.reality: It opens with a row of label:value dropdown controls (Sort by: Most recent, View mode: Grid 3 col), then a three-column grid. Each item carries a meta line of date plus byline, a headline, and a small category chip beneath it. The grid images are square-cornered, unlike the rounded media elsewhere on the site.
corrections.impact: Blog index rebuilt. The square-cornered grid images were NOT adopted — see `deliberateDivergences`.

clientDirection.softness: Match T1 fully. Pill nav and buttons, 32px radius on media and cards, circular icon buttons. Square corners leave the system.
clientDirection.labelCase: Keep sentence case. CLAUDE.md §7 stands. The mono face carries the technical register instead of capitals — the point where this design deliberately diverges from the reference.
clientDirection.colour: Blue on links and CTAs only. Pages read monochrome. No navy institutional bands.
clientDirection.density: Follow T1's spacing and accept longer pages. Required footnotes, 'as of' stamps and source lines sit small in the empty column — the space is where provenance lives.
clientDirection.actionColour: #0C73CD, supplied 2026-09-13. Pinned at blue/600 and the blue ramp is regenerated around it. It replaces the seed blue #3F74AB as the anchor of the blue family; the seed blue now has no semantic role and needs a decision.
clientDirection.labelMark: No mark before section labels. The reference's small filled square was built across the file and removed at the client's direction on 2026-09-13 — 38 instances across components, page comps and the foundations board. Labels are mono text alone.
clientDirection.gridAndRhythm: Stats are gridded, not stacked. Sections are broken before they run long, and full-bleed imagery separates them. Applied 2026-09-13: the homepage stat stack split into two gridded sections, the Workforce figures regridded three-up, and five image bands added across Home, Workforce, The Campus, Community and FAQ.
clientDirection.imageryAndResponsive: Placeholder imagery applied across all photographic slots 2026-09-13, using the client-supplied hero image. Logo, map and blocked-content slots deliberately stay flat grey — a photograph there would misrepresent what is actually missing. A full 375px mobile set was derived for all seven pages.
clientDirection.desktopRevision: Client art-directed the desktop file directly on 2026-09-13 and asked for the changes to be rippled out. Four edits, all made at the token or component layer, so they had already reached every desktop instance: button padding re-pointed to space/8 vertical (43px tall desktop, 41 mobile); the nav capsule moved off radius/pill to a 16px radius and its panel from 62% to 50%; the hero headline re-bound from display to font-size/h2; and dark surface/inverse bands painted into the page rhythm. Two further edits did not survive review: action/primary-bg and text/link were both re-pointed to blue/500, which fails AA as a button fill (3.42:1 with a white label) and on the page ground (2.92:1). blue/500 was kept where it does clear — text/link-inverse on the dark bands, 4.92:1 — and the fill and light-ground link returned to blue/600 and blue/700.
clientDirection.sectionRhythm: Colour breaks the scroll. Light ink/100 ground is the default; surface/inverse bands and full-bleed photography alternate into it so no two reading sections sit adjacent. Home runs photo → ground → photo → ground → dark → ground → photo → ground → ground → dark → ground → dark footer. Inner pages open dark: page top and page hero are one continuous surface/inverse block under the floating nav.
clientDirection.timelineRevision: Supplied 2026-09-14 as a reference frame: a vertical centred spine, date pills sitting on the axis, content alternating left and right of it, and one marker carrying an accent while the rest sit quiet. Applied to both timelines and to the 375px set. Two things could not be copied literally. The reference's accent is a warm orange; blue here means link and no second signal colour is signed off (open questions 16 and 18), so the loud/quiet ramp is carried by the ink ramp instead — ink/950 pill and rail on the most recent milestone, ink/750 on the rest. And the reference sets its item titles in all-caps, which CLAUDE.md §7 forbids; they stay sentence case.

openGround.name: Open ground
openGround.definition: There is no container system. Content sits on one continuous warm off-white ground, separated by vertical space and by the asymmetric grid.
theOnlyFilledSurfaces: The floating nav pill (translucent over media)
rules: No cards on the page ground. No tinted bands. No rules or dividers between sections.
A section states one thing, and is separated from the next by section-y (160px).
Provenance — footnote, source, "as of" date — sits in the empty column beside the thing it qualifies, never pooled at the page foot.

deliberateDivergences.reference: Section and stat labels set in mono ALL-CAPS, preceded by a small filled square.
deliberateDivergences.ours: Mono face, sentence case, no preceding mark.
deliberateDivergences.why: CLAUDE.md §7 forbids all-caps and the client chose to keep that rule. The square bullet was built and then removed at the client's direction — it was the last decorative mark in the system, and the mono face already does the work of separating a label from body copy.

deliberateDivergences.reference: Dimmed mega-menu child items sit at roughly 3.4:1 against the panel.
deliberateDivergences.ours: Panel ground darkened from 0.62 to 0.86 alpha so dimmed children reach 6.10:1.
deliberateDivergences.why: The visual hierarchy is preserved; the accessibility failure is not. WCAG 2.2 AA is non-negotiable for a public information site.

deliberateDivergences.ours: Blog images take radius/media (32) like every other photograph.
deliberateDivergences.why: P4 makes radius the system-wide expression of softness, and the client chose to match it fully. A single square-cornered grid would read as a bug rather than a decision. One token flips this if the client prefers the reference.

deliberateDivergences.reference: Numeric dates (09.04.26) and a personal byline (Posted by <author>).
deliberateDivergences.ours: Spelled-out dates (4 September 2026) and the issuing organisation in the byline slot.
deliberateDivergences.why: CLAUDE.md §9 requires plain language — a numeric date is ambiguous and slower to read. Press releases have no author; for supportive coverage the outlet is the thing worth crediting, and crediting it is part of the transparency argument.

deliberateDivergences.reference: Facility pages named with underscore codes (G1_Dallas, G2_Austin, HQ_Austin).
deliberateDivergences.why: The convention encodes T1's multi-facility structure. Homer City is one site; borrowing the codes would imply a scale that does not exist.

deliberateDivergences.reference: The live timeline milestone is marked in warm orange — pill and rail — and past milestones drop to grey along with their body copy.
deliberateDivergences.ours: The current milestone takes an ink/950 pill and rail and past ones ink/750. Body copy stays text/secondary throughout.
deliberateDivergences.why: Blue is the only colour in this system and it means link (CLAUDE.md §7); no second signal colour is signed off (open questions 16 and 18). The ink ramp carries the same loud-to-quiet ramp without inventing a hue. Dimming the body of past milestones would dim the evidence on a site whose whole job is transparency — so only the marker changes.

informationArchitecture.readingOfTheReference: Five top-level items. Three are parents holding children grouped by kind, two are external destinations marked with a trailing arrow and placed last. The blog sits under a parent rather than in the bar. Children are revealed in the expanded panel, never as a flat list.
informationArchitecture.changeFromStage2: This regroups the approved Stage 2 sitemap. FAQ & Resources and News were separate top-level items; they now sit together under a Newsroom parent, which is where a sceptic's whole journey — the answer, the release, the filing — lives in one place. Flagged for the client rather than assumed.
informationArchitecture.panelCTAs: Jobs (light, filled) and Get in touch (translucent). Jobs leads — the reference puts Get in touch first, but the brief says put as much focus as possible on workforce.
informationArchitecture.externalMarker: A trailing ↗ marks anything leaving the site. Permits & filings points at PA DEP, which is the point: the sceptic should be able to reach the primary source, not our description of it.
informationArchitecture.unresolved: The nav now declares children that do not all exist as separate comps. In the reference, 'Overview' as a first child implies each parent is a hub with real child pages. Here, most children (Power block, Water & site, Timeline, Trades on site, Apprenticeships, How to apply) are currently sections inside their parent page — which is defensible given the client chose the reference's long-page spacing, and would make them anchor links rather than routes. Decide which: anchor links keep seven pages, separate routes adds roughly ten more and changes the URL map in docs/02-plan.md §2.

responsive.principle: Everything is auto-layout. Nothing is positioned absolutely except elements that float over hero media — the logo, the nav capsule, the Jobs pill, the hero copy block and the announcement card. Every other frame is a stack or a row that reflows.
howMobileDerives: Wide rows become stacks. Any horizontal auto-layout spanning more than ~300px of content flips to vertical; pills, meta lines, marks and button groups stay horizontal.
Wrapped grids become single columns. layoutWrap is switched off and the frame becomes vertical, so nothing depends on a cell width that no longer fits.
Every stack hugs its content. This is the failure that clips things: a frame converted from wrap keeps its old fixed height and silently crops the items below the fold.
Anything pinned wider than the 343px content column becomes FILL.
Desktop-tall media (440-560px) is capped to 240px so a photograph does not eat the whole screen.
Section margins go 80 to 16; section padding goes 120-160 to 64.

A FILL child inside a column that hugs has nothing to fill, and Figma resolves it by freezing the child's height and clipping. This is the quiet one: 35 frames were affected, and eight of them had collapsed to 1px — three of four project pillars, three of four sequence steps and two of three news items were invisible on mobile while the section around them looked finished. Audit by comparing every clipping frame's content bottom against its height, not by eye.
mobileSpecifics: The nav capsule is replaced by a Menu pill. The Jobs button stays in the bar beside it — the brief is explicit that the one thing a tradesperson came for is never behind a toggle.
Hero scrim goes to 0.88-0.92 throughout rather than a horizontal ramp, because the text column spans the full width.
The announcement card keeps copy and thumbnail side by side but drops the thumbnail to 96px; the card hugs, so two stack inside an 800px hero.
Stats are one per row, and the blank qualifier line that holds the desktop baseline is dropped — with a single column there is no row to align to.
Button labels hug. A label left at FILL in a 145px column wraps to two lines and doubles the button's height.

The timeline spine moves from centre to left. The rail sits at x=16, which is exactly the centre of the date pill's left cap, so the two stay aligned whatever the date string; copy indents 20px from the rail and fills the rest of the column. Alternating sides would leave about 145px per side at 375.
responsive.typography: Only font size varies by breakpoint, carried by the Typography collection Desktop/Mobile modes and set on the artboard. Line height and tracking are percentages and scale on their own.
